$what: connection:press-fit-tube-15 — the Ø15 arch cradle and the ring it holds, frozen from cecad.meshslice circle fits, cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders and cecad.meshfeatures.intervals on Pollen's meshes (metres, scale 1000), 2026-09-02, ce-designs/microduck lane T

host.frame: the mesh frame of motor_support.stl: x -39.5..34.0, y -26.2..28.0, z 0.4..19.2; the cradle axis is the x-line through (y 0, z 7.4995)

relief_d_basis.why_this_replaced_16.8: the value written here on 2026-09-02 was 16.8 — one decimal place in a file whose every other dimension carries four, and the house rule is 3–4 dp with the tolerance basis stated. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-03 (lane T fix pass) off the mesh VERTICES rather than off a ray, because a ray through a tessellated bore reads the facet, not the cylinder.
relief_d_basis.method: every vertex of motor_support.stl (scale 1000) with radius 8.30–8.50 mm about the cradle axis (y 0, z 7.4995) and x in -37.6..-36.4 — the relief band and nothing else. n = 64 vertices, in two rings of 32 at x -37.5000 and x -36.5000; no vertex row exists between them, so the surface is a straight cylinder over its whole length.
relief_d_basis.tolerance_basis: 1 sigma = 0.000247 mm on the diameter over 64 vertices; the full spread max-min is 0.0008 mm. That scatter is the STL’s float32 storage, not a shape: the design nominal is Ø16.8000 and the mesh carries it to +0.0007 mm.
relief_d_basis.why_a_ray_reads_less: the bore is a 32-facet chord polygon over the 152.4451° that exists; its vertices lie ON the cylinder and every facet lies INSIDE it by up to one sagitta, 0.00773 mm. A ray-cast caliper that crosses a facet near its centre therefore reads Ø16.7852, and cecad.meshslice.intervals() rounds its returns to 3 dp on top of that. An independent check on 2026-09-03 read r 8.3928 → Ø16.7856 at x -37.0 by exactly that route; it is the SAME surface measured through a chord, and it agrees with the mid-chord prediction to 0.0004 mm. The vertex figure is the one that describes the cylinder.
relief_d_basis.cross_check: the same vertex method on the Ø15 ring-band bore (r 7.45–7.55, x -39.8..-35.3, n = 124 at x -39.5000/-37.5000/-36.5000/-35.5000) reads Ø15.0007, sd 0.000237 — the same +0.0007 mm float32 offset from its own Ø15.0000 nominal, which is what makes the offset a storage artefact rather than a feature.
relief_d_basis.measured: 2026-09-03, cecad.meshslice.load + numpy on the mesh vertices; script out/laneT/remeasure_relief.py, output out/laneT/relief-remeasure.json

host.how_bands_were_read: cecad.meshfeatures.intervals(motor_support, axis x, y=0, z=15.6) — a line at radius 8.100 mm from the cradle axis, inside the Ø17.39 outer surface and outside the Ø15.0 bore: material exists only where the ring band exists
host.open_angle_why: 360 - 149.06: the arch is cut off flat at z 9.5000 and there is NO material below that plane at these x stations (cecad.meshslice section at x=-38.5 spans z 9.5000..16.1919 only). The cradle is a hook, not a bore.

placed_in_host_frame.how: the MJCF body/geom frames of robot_allcollisions.xml composed at zero pose, then expressed in the motor_support mesh frame (cecad.mjcf.bodies_world + quat_to_mat)

guest_journal.how_journal_span_was_read: cecad.meshfeatures.intervals(jaw, axis x) at (y 4.9, z 7.5) -> [-43.732, -37.0] (inside the Ø10 journal) and at (y 5.5, z 7.5) -> [-43.707, -39.7] (outside it): the journal proper is x -39.7000..-37.0000

coaxiality_mm.why: the cradle bore centre reads z 7.4995 (best station, residual mean 0.00352 mm) and the jaw journal centre reads z 7.5000 exactly (residual max 0.00254 mm) — the two PARTS are coaxial to 0.0005 mm. Pollen's MJCF places the bearing GEOM's axis at z 7.7000, 0.2005 mm above both, and 0.3000 mm outboard of the journal shoulder. That is a discrepancy in the visual placement of the model, not in the two parts' geometry, and it is recorded here rather than averaged away.
